Generated from the clap definition of the `canon` command line in [`crates/canon-cli/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/canon/blob/main/crates/canon-cli/src/lib.rs). It lists only commands that exist; commands the design proposes are on the [status page](../status/where-this-stands.md).

`canon`: Evidence-governed protocol toolchain. `canon --version` prints its version, and `--help` after any command prints the text shown below.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`canon validate`](#canon-validate) | Parse and validate a `protocol/1` document, composed with the documents it imports |
| [`canon compile`](#canon-compile) | Compile a valid `protocol/1` document, composed with the documents it imports, into one closed `canon-ir/1` and print it |
| [`canon evaluate`](#canon-evaluate) | Evaluate a case under a compiled protocol from an evidence set: every claim, and each declared obligation, action and outcome. Print the `canon-decision/1` document |
| [`canon check`](#canon-check) | Check a `protocol/1` document over its whole finite state space: report outcomes no state reaches, actions whose precondition holds in no state, claims, obligations, preconditions and outcome requirements that read evidence no action produces and no other protocol supplies, outcomes that rest on evidence an authority-requiring action may produce yet hold without any authority decision, and each declared property that fails, with a counterexample. An evidence kind that declares `supplied_by` counts as produced without authority and stays governed when an action that requires a capability may also produce it, so an outcome a supplied record alone makes legitimate is reported as a bypass. A state is a set of evidence records, authority decisions and explicit decisions; a record an invalidation rule can keep from a claim is there in any combination of observed before and after each upstream artifact moved, one record each. Evidence an order form reads (`first`, `before`, `after`, `since`) is also there with earlier records at a superseded revision, or with no known instant, in every order of first observations; evidence an `after` or a `since` compares with its result also with a later record of that result, placed anywhere in that order or at no known instant; and evidence a `since` reads as its last kind also with a last record at a superseded revision, placed in that order on its own, with or just after its own first observations or a later record it is compared with. Evidence an evidence match demanding independence reads (`independent_on`) is there from a producer independent on exactly each demand, in every combination of demands met, and without a producer when something that demands nothing reads it. Evidence a `children` form reads (`case_outcome`) is also there with earlier records at a superseded revision, each record the outcome of a child case of its own, and with no place in the order, which the form does not read; an action that opens a child case (`case_open`) counts as producing `case_outcome` about its `case_open` subject when the protocol reads `case_outcome` about that artifact by name, in a `children` form or an evidence match, otherwise without a subject, and a `children` form naming a `subject` reads only records about it; and a protocol that reads `case_outcome` with both a `children` form and an order form is refused (`ordered-child-outcomes`). Each outcome, action and property is decided over the evidence, authority, decisions and case inputs it reads (its slice), with the findings and witness states the whole state space gives, and the summary counts the whole state space; a check in which one slice holds more than 65536 states is refused, naming that outcome, action or property and the slice's dimensions, and a whole state space too large to count is refused naming the whole state space and its dimensions |
| [`canon simulate`](#canon-simulate) | Walk every state a case of a `protocol/1` document can reach from the empty case, one step at a time, and report the states no sequence of steps gets out of, each action admissible in no reachable state, and each outcome legitimate in no reachable state. A step adds one current record an admissible action may produce (`may_produce`), or one of each kind of a group the action records together (`records_together`), never one of those kinds alone, moves a non-empty subset of the artifacts an admissible action declares in `revises` to a new revision, alone or with one such record or group added at the new revision (a revise step, tried after the action's record steps, subsets in order of their sorted ids, written `action x revises a` or `action x revises a and produces …`), adds one record of a kind that declares `supplied_by` (at any step), adds one child case's `case_outcome` record, lets one record class of a kind that declares `max_age` expire, grants or denies one capability some action requires, or takes one decision some outcome requires; no action runs. Since a step adds one record outside a group, where an action's guard closes on its first record the walk never holds two records of one taking together unless the action declares them a group, and an outcome that needs both is reported as legitimate in no reachable state. Per action that opens a child case (`case_open`) the walk counts the children that have not ended: none, one, or two or more. A step of the action raises the count, a child's outcome arrives while it is above none, and an outcome other than `open` lowers it, or from two or more may also leave it at two or more, and replaces an `open` record, since one record is one child. A child of an opening action records `case_outcome` about the artifact the action's `case_open` names when the protocol reads `case_outcome` about that artifact by name, otherwise without a subject. A state holding an `open` record, current or held as expired, keeps the count of some action that produces that record above none, because an `open` record is a child that has not ended. A state names each action with a count above none (`action a opened a child`, `action a opened 2 or more children`). An expired `case_outcome` record still counts for a `children` form: with no evidence match reading `case_outcome` it does not expire, and otherwise it is held as expired, absent to every evidence match. A revision of an artifact removes the current records about it, except that a `case_outcome` record a `children` form reads becomes an earlier record (written `earlier`), which a `children` form without `revision: current` still reads, and turns a record with that artifact upstream into one observed before it moved (written `observed before upstream a moved`), which its invalidation rules keep from their claims. A state holds no revision number, and the case revision never moves: capability and taken decisions stay, so a denial lasts. The records of a kind no match names an artifact for are taken to be about the first artifact no match of the kind names. An action without `revises` has no revise step. A state is open when action (record and revise), supplied, child-outcome, expiry and authority steps lead from it to a legitimate outcome; decisions do not count. A state that is not open is a stuck state when no action is admissible or approval-required, and a cycle when no action is approval-required and every record step of every admissible action returns the same state; when a revise step leads out of a cycle, it says every record step and ends `every revision by action x leads to a state no outcome is reachable from`. Each is printed once, at its smallest state, with the shortest path that reaches it, each decision that would make an outcome legitimate there, and how many other such states contain it; an open state in which no outcome is legitimate, no action is approval-required, and every step of every admissible action, record or revise, returns the state is counted as waiting. The summary counts the reachable states, per outcome those in which it is legitimate, the waiting states, the findings and the stuck and cycle states they stand for. A protocol with an order form (`first`, `before`, `after`, `since`) is refused (`ordered-evidence`), and so is a walk that would visit more than 65536 states (`reachable-state-bound`), which reports nothing of what it saw |
| [`canon generate`](#canon-generate) | Generate `canon-conformance/1` scenarios into an empty directory: one minimal witness per declared outcome and per action blocked in some state, over the whole state space that `canon check` covers. Each names the protocol path, as given, as its fixture, so `canon conform run` runs them from the working directory `canon generate` ran in. Refused, writing nothing: a protocol path that resolves outside the working directory, an outcome no state reaches, a protocol that yields no scenario, an outcome or action identifier holding a character a file name cannot hold (`/ \ : * ? " < > \|` or a control character), two scenario file names equal up to letter case or Unicode normalisation, a protocol with imports (a scenario names one fixture), a non-empty `--out`, and a whole state space of more than 65536 states, which `canon check` may still decide slice by slice. On failure, nothing this run created is left |
| [`canon diff`](#canon-diff) | The semantic difference between two compiled revisions of one protocol: every change, each classified as `TIGHTENING`, `RELAXATION`, `BREAKING`, `EXPANSION` or `NO SEMANTIC CHANGE` and naming the identifiers it touches. Two revisions of different protocols are refused |
| [`canon conform`](#canon-conform) | Conformance scenarios |
| [`canon conform run`](#canon-conform-run) | Run every `canon-conformance/1` scenario of a registry directory and report each |

## `canon validate`

Parse and validate a `protocol/1` document, composed with the documents it imports

| Option | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--path <PATH>` | yes | none | The protocol document to validate |
| `--import <IMPORT>` | no | none | A `protocol/1` document the protocol imports, directly or through another import. Repeat it once per document, in any order; each import is checked against its pinned revision and digest. Without it, a protocol with imports is refused |

```text
Parse and validate a `protocol/1` document, composed with the documents it imports

Usage: canon validate [OPTIONS] --path <PATH>

Options:
      --path <PATH>
          The protocol document to validate

      --import <IMPORT>
          A `protocol/1` document the protocol imports, directly or through another import. Repeat it once per document, in any order; each import is checked against its pinned revision and digest. Without it, a protocol with imports is refused

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `canon compile`

Compile a valid `protocol/1` document, composed with the documents it imports, into one closed `canon-ir/1` and print it

| Option | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--path <PATH>` | yes | none | The protocol document to compile |
| `--import <IMPORT>` | no | none | A `protocol/1` document the protocol imports, directly or through another import. Repeat it once per document, in any order: the order changes no byte of the IR |

```text
Compile a valid `protocol/1` document, composed with the documents it imports, into one closed `canon-ir/1` and print it

Usage: canon compile [OPTIONS] --path <PATH>

Options:
      --path <PATH>
          The protocol document to compile

      --import <IMPORT>
          A `protocol/1` document the protocol imports, directly or through another import. Repeat it once per document, in any order: the order changes no byte of the IR

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `canon evaluate`

Evaluate a case under a compiled protocol from an evidence set: every claim, and each declared obligation, action and outcome. Print the `canon-decision/1` document

| Option | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--ir <IR>` | yes | none | The compiled protocol: `canon-ir/1` exactly as `canon compile` prints it |
| `--case <CASE>` | yes | none | The `canon-case/1` case snapshot |
| `--evidence <EVIDENCE>` | yes | none | A directory holding only `canon-evidence/1` records, one per `*.yaml` or `*.json` file |
| `--authority <AUTHORITY>` | no | none | A `canon-authority/1` document: which capabilities are granted, granted only with approval or denied, each at a scope or at every scope. An action is admissible only when every capability it requires is granted at the scope it requires it; without it, none is granted. A decision that gives a case revision applies only while the case snapshot is at that revision; its principal is recorded as given |
| `--decisions <DECISIONS>` | no | none | A `canon-decisions/1` document: the explicit decisions taken, each naming the decision, the outcome, the principal and the case revision it was taken at. An outcome that requires a decision is legitimate only with one taken at the case snapshot's revision |
| `--at <AT>` | no | none | The evaluation instant, in UTC as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffZ` with one to nine fraction digits. Evidence older than its kind's `max_age` at this instant, counted in whole seconds, does not apply; without it, no evidence expires |

```text
Evaluate a case under a compiled protocol from an evidence set: every claim, and each declared obligation, action and outcome. Print the `canon-decision/1` document

Usage: canon evaluate [OPTIONS] --ir <IR> --case <CASE> --evidence <EVIDENCE>

Options:
      --ir <IR>
          The compiled protocol: `canon-ir/1` exactly as `canon compile` prints it

      --case <CASE>
          The `canon-case/1` case snapshot

      --evidence <EVIDENCE>
          A directory holding only `canon-evidence/1` records, one per `*.yaml` or `*.json` file

      --authority <AUTHORITY>
          A `canon-authority/1` document: which capabilities are granted, granted only with approval or denied, each at a scope or at every scope. An action is admissible only when every capability it requires is granted at the scope it requires it; without it, none is granted. A decision that gives a case revision applies only while the case snapshot is at that revision; its principal is recorded as given

      --decisions <DECISIONS>
          A `canon-decisions/1` document: the explicit decisions taken, each naming the decision, the outcome, the principal and the case revision it was taken at. An outcome that requires a decision is legitimate only with one taken at the case snapshot's revision

      --at <AT>
          The evaluation instant, in UTC as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`, or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.fffZ` with one to nine fraction digits. Evidence older than its kind's `max_age` at this instant, counted in whole seconds, does not apply; without it, no evidence expires

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `canon check`

Check a `protocol/1` document over its whole finite state space: report outcomes no state reaches, actions whose precondition holds in no state, claims, obligations, preconditions and outcome requirements that read evidence no action produces and no other protocol supplies, outcomes that rest on evidence an authority-requiring action may produce yet hold without any authority decision, and each declared property that fails, with a counterexample. An evidence kind that declares `supplied_by` counts as produced without authority and stays governed when an action that requires a capability may also produce it, so an outcome a supplied record alone makes legitimate is reported as a bypass. A state is a set of evidence records, authority decisions and explicit decisions; a record an invalidation rule can keep from a claim is there in any combination of observed before and after each upstream artifact moved, one record each. Evidence an order form reads (`first`, `before`, `after`, `since`) is also there with earlier records at a superseded revision, or with no known instant, in every order of first observations; evidence an `after` or a `since` compares with its result also with a later record of that result, placed anywhere in that order or at no known instant; and evidence a `since` reads as its last kind also with a last record at a superseded revision, placed in that order on its own, with or just after its own first observations or a later record it is compared with. Evidence an evidence match demanding independence reads (`independent_on`) is there from a producer independent on exactly each demand, in every combination of demands met, and without a producer when something that demands nothing reads it. Evidence a `children` form reads (`case_outcome`) is also there with earlier records at a superseded revision, each record the outcome of a child case of its own, and with no place in the order, which the form does not read; an action that opens a child case (`case_open`) counts as producing `case_outcome` about its `case_open` subject when the protocol reads `case_outcome` about that artifact by name, in a `children` form or an evidence match, otherwise without a subject, and a `children` form naming a `subject` reads only records about it; and a protocol that reads `case_outcome` with both a `children` form and an order form is refused (`ordered-child-outcomes`). Each outcome, action and property is decided over the evidence, authority, decisions and case inputs it reads (its slice), with the findings and witness states the whole state space gives, and the summary counts the whole state space; a check in which one slice holds more than 65536 states is refused, naming that outcome, action or property and the slice's dimensions, and a whole state space too large to count is refused naming the whole state space and its dimensions

| Option | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--path <PATH>` | yes | none | The protocol document to check |
| `--properties <PROPERTIES>` | no | none | A `canon-properties/1` document: properties declared beside the protocol, each saying an action's or outcome's status is independent of a claim. Each is checked in every state |
| `--import <IMPORT>` | no | none | A `protocol/1` document the protocol imports, directly or through another import. Repeat it once per document, in any order; the protocol is checked composed with them |

```text
Check a `protocol/1` document over its whole finite state space: report outcomes no state reaches, actions whose precondition holds in no state, claims, obligations, preconditions and outcome requirements that read evidence no action produces and no other protocol supplies, outcomes that rest on evidence an authority-requiring action may produce yet hold without any authority decision, and each declared property that fails, with a counterexample. An evidence kind that declares `supplied_by` counts as produced without authority and stays governed when an action that requires a capability may also produce it, so an outcome a supplied record alone makes legitimate is reported as a bypass. A state is a set of evidence records, authority decisions and explicit decisions; a record an invalidation rule can keep from a claim is there in any combination of observed before and after each upstream artifact moved, one record each. Evidence an order form reads (`first`, `before`, `after`, `since`) is also there with earlier records at a superseded revision, or with no known instant, in every order of first observations; evidence an `after` or a `since` compares with its result also with a later record of that result, placed anywhere in that order or at no known instant; and evidence a `since` reads as its last kind also with a last record at a superseded revision, placed in that order on its own, with or just after its own first observations or a later record it is compared with. Evidence an evidence match demanding independence reads (`independent_on`) is there from a producer independent on exactly each demand, in every combination of demands met, and without a producer when something that demands nothing reads it. Evidence a `children` form reads (`case_outcome`) is also there with earlier records at a superseded revision, each record the outcome of a child case of its own, and with no place in the order, which the form does not read; an action that opens a child case (`case_open`) counts as producing `case_outcome` about its `case_open` subject when the protocol reads `case_outcome` about that artifact by name, in a `children` form or an evidence match, otherwise without a subject, and a `children` form naming a `subject` reads only records about it; and a protocol that reads `case_outcome` with both a `children` form and an order form is refused (`ordered-child-outcomes`). Each outcome, action and property is decided over the evidence, authority, decisions and case inputs it reads (its slice), with the findings and witness states the whole state space gives, and the summary counts the whole state space; a check in which one slice holds more than 65536 states is refused, naming that outcome, action or property and the slice's dimensions, and a whole state space too large to count is refused naming the whole state space and its dimensions

Usage: canon check [OPTIONS] --path <PATH>

Options:
      --path <PATH>
          The protocol document to check

      --properties <PROPERTIES>
          A `canon-properties/1` document: properties declared beside the protocol, each saying an action's or outcome's status is independent of a claim. Each is checked in every state

      --import <IMPORT>
          A `protocol/1` document the protocol imports, directly or through another import. Repeat it once per document, in any order; the protocol is checked composed with them

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `canon generate`

Generate `canon-conformance/1` scenarios into an empty directory: one minimal witness per declared outcome and per action blocked in some state, over the whole state space that `canon check` covers. Each names the protocol path, as given, as its fixture, so `canon conform run` runs them from the working directory `canon generate` ran in. Refused, writing nothing: a protocol path that resolves outside the working directory, an outcome no state reaches, a protocol that yields no scenario, an outcome or action identifier holding a character a file name cannot hold (`/ \ : * ? " < > \|` or a control character), two scenario file names equal up to letter case or Unicode normalisation, a protocol with imports (a scenario names one fixture), a non-empty `--out`, and a whole state space of more than 65536 states, which `canon check` may still decide slice by slice. On failure, nothing this run created is left

| Option | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--path <PATH>` | yes | none | The protocol document, as a relative path without `..` components |
| `--out <OUT>` | yes | none | The directory to write the scenarios to: absent or empty. When absent it is created, with any missing parents; an existing one, or a symbolic link to one, is written into as it is |

```text
Generate `canon-conformance/1` scenarios into an empty directory: one minimal witness per declared outcome and per action blocked in some state, over the whole state space that `canon check` covers. Each names the protocol path, as given, as its fixture, so `canon conform run` runs them from the working directory `canon generate` ran in. Refused, writing nothing: a protocol path that resolves outside the working directory, an outcome no state reaches, a protocol that yields no scenario, an outcome or action identifier holding a character a file name cannot hold (`/ \ : * ? " < > |` or a control character), two scenario file names equal up to letter case or Unicode normalisation, a protocol with imports (a scenario names one fixture), a non-empty `--out`, and a whole state space of more than 65536 states, which `canon check` may still decide slice by slice. On failure, nothing this run created is left

Usage: canon generate --path <PATH> --out <OUT>

Options:
      --path <PATH>
          The protocol document, as a relative path without `..` components

      --out <OUT>
          The directory to write the scenarios to: absent or empty. When absent it is created, with any missing parents; an existing one, or a symbolic link to one, is written into as it is

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `canon diff`

The semantic difference between two compiled revisions of one protocol: every change, each classified as `TIGHTENING`, `RELAXATION`, `BREAKING`, `EXPANSION` or `NO SEMANTIC CHANGE` and naming the identifiers it touches. Two revisions of different protocols are refused

| Option | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--from <FROM>` | yes | none | The earlier revision, as `canon compile` prints it |
| `--to <TO>` | yes | none | The later revision, as `canon compile` prints it |

```text
The semantic difference between two compiled revisions of one protocol: every change, each classified as `TIGHTENING`, `RELAXATION`, `BREAKING`, `EXPANSION` or `NO SEMANTIC CHANGE` and naming the identifiers it touches. Two revisions of different protocols are refused

Usage: canon diff --from <FROM> --to <TO>

Options:
      --from <FROM>
          The earlier revision, as `canon compile` prints it

      --to <TO>
          The later revision, as `canon compile` prints it

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `canon conform`

Conformance scenarios

Subcommands: [`run`](#canon-conform-run).

Conformance scenarios

  run   Run every `canon-conformance/1` scenario of a registry directory and report each

Options:

          Print help

## `canon conform run`

Run every `canon-conformance/1` scenario of a registry directory and report each

| Option | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--scenarios <SCENARIOS>` | no | `conformance/scenarios` | The registry directory; every `*.yaml` file in it is one scenario |
| `--requirements <REQUIREMENTS>` | no | none | A `canon-requirements/1` catalogue of the normative requirements the registry answers for. After the run, every implemented requirement must be covered by a passing scenario, no scenario may cover one the catalogue does not list, no planned one may be covered, and every evaluate step must give byte-identical output when run again and with its `evidence`, `authority` and `decisions` lists reversed. Adds a `requirements:` summary line |

```text
Run every `canon-conformance/1` scenario of a registry directory and report each

Usage: canon conform run [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --scenarios <SCENARIOS>
          The registry directory; every `*.yaml` file in it is one scenario

          [default: conformance/scenarios]

      --requirements <REQUIREMENTS>
          A `canon-requirements/1` catalogue of the normative requirements the registry answers for. After the run, every implemented requirement must be covered by a passing scenario, no scenario may cover one the catalogue does not list, no planned one may be covered, and every evaluate step must give byte-identical output when run again and with its `evidence`, `authority` and `decisions` lists reversed. Adds a `requirements:` summary line

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## Exit status

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | Success: the document is valid or compiled, the case was evaluated, every conformance scenario ran and passed, a check or a simulation found nothing, or the scenarios were generated. |
| `1` | Rejected: a document was read and rejected, an evaluation, a check or a simulation was refused, a conformance scenario failed or was unreadable, no scenario ran, a requirement check failed, a check or a simulation found something, or generation was refused. |
| `2` | Unreadable: an input file or directory could not be read, or an output file could not be written. |
| `64` | Usage error: the command line was not understood (an unknown command or option, a missing required option, or a value that cannot be parsed); nothing was read. |
